front:
Edit the provided image locally, as a precise-object-edit. It is a locked 1024 x 1024 orthographic FRONT template for fitting a game armor piece onto an existing 3D mannequin. Produce ONE image only: this exact front template wearing ONE open-face helmet.

The input image is the editing target, not inspiration for drawing another character. Keep the blue mannequin at its exact current coordinates, scale, A-pose, silhouette and original blue color. Preserve the entire original light gray background and framing. Preserve all pixels outside the head/helmet area as closely as possible. Do not change the shoulders, neck, body, arms, hands, legs or feet. Do not add a face, eyes, nose, mouth, hair, other armor, weapon, shadow on the ground, lettering or a second view. No pixelation.

ONLY ADD THIS HELMET: a carefully fitted, symmetrical, open-faced dark-fantasy steel helmet. Its smooth dome hugs the existing oversized head with a small uniform clearance. It covers the skull crown, the rear skull and both sides of the head down to chin level, enclosing the ears. The blue central front of the mannequin's featureless face must remain clearly visible through a large open face opening. No visor, mask, mouth guard, beard, plume, horns or decoration extending above the dome. Side/cheek guards belong to the same simple helmet shell, ending at the mannequin's chin level, not overlapping the neck or shoulders. Never shrink or reshape the blue head to fit the armor.

Design: strong, simple rounded steel shell, with one broad gold band running along the center of the dome from front to rear and a broad understated gold trim tracing the open face rim and lower edges. Neutral dark charcoal/steel GRAY metal, muted antique GOLD trim. Absolutely NO blue hue in the added helmet, even its highlights: the underlying mannequin alone remains blue for color segmentation. Use big clean forms readable on a ~70px-high game character. Sword of Convallaria-inspired dark fantasy proportions, but render the added helmet cleanly and smoothly at this template's original resolution, matching its soft upper-front illumination. No black outlines, tiny rivets, engravings, realistic gritty texture, mirror highlights or harsh cast shadows.

Geometry placement guide on this image: blue skull top about y=103, chin about y=336, ears x=401..623; torso/shoulders start below y=345. Use only a few pixels of clearance beyond the blue head. The steel-and-gold helmet must visually be a wearable thin-shell object over this exact head, not a floating giant helmet and not embedded into the skull. Keep the overall image exactly 1024x1024.
back_initial:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Produce ONE orthographic BACK view armor-fitting image, not a collage.

Input image 1 is the LOCKED BACK TEMPLATE and the sole editing target: the faceless blue game mannequin seen directly from behind, in an A-pose, on a light gray background.
Input image 2 is SUPPORTING HELMET DESIGN REFERENCE ONLY: the same mannequin wearing the helmet seen from the front. Use only its helmet design. Do not copy its front-facing blue body or face, do not introduce a front opening on the back.

Edit image 1 by adding ONLY the rear view of EXACTLY THE SAME HELMET shown in image 2. Maintain image 1's exact body coordinates, size, silhouette, pose, blue color, shoulders, neck, arms, hands, torso, legs, feet, light gray background and 1024 x 1024 framing. All areas outside the helmet must remain unchanged. No new character, no rotation, no perspective, no pixelization, no text, no weapons, no other clothing/armor, no hair, no face or floor shadow.

The matching helmet has a close-fitting rounded dark steel-gray dome, broad muted gold band centered over the skull from front to back, broad gold lower rim, and plain cheek/ear side guards. In this DIRECT REAR VIEW, the helmet fully covers the back of the blue skull and ears down to the original chin-height plane. The gold band continues down the center of the rear dome and joins the gold bottom rim. Back rim forms a clean fitted rounded edge above the visible blue neck. It must not extend onto shoulders or torso. From behind there is NO face opening: the broad steel shell is continuous over the entire back of the head. Matching side guards may appear at the left and right edges, in an exactly symmetrical silhouette. No extra embellishments, crests, horns, plume, buckles, tiny rivets, engraving or ornate lines.

Fit the shell to the existing head with only a few pixels of uniform clearance. Do not shrink the head, alter the body proportions, float the helmet above it or sink metal into the skull. On input image 1 the skull begins about y=103, the original chin/neck line is about y=336, shoulders start below y=345. The helmet outer contour should conform to this same head envelope. Retain the current soft upper-front lighting in the template with gentle shading. Clean smooth dark-fantasy stylized painting, large readable forms inspired by Sword of Convallaria, no black outlines, no gritty texture, no harsh cast shadow or blown specular. Neutral CHARCOAL/GRAY steel and muted GOLD only in the helmet, ABSOLUTELY NO BLUE in any metal, shadows or highlights; only the unchanged underlying mannequin is blue.

The visual design, dome size, center band width, bottom gold rim width and metal color must match the FRONT helmet in input image 2, seen accurately from behind. Export exactly one 1024 x 1024 PNG.
back_alignment_correction:
Precise-object-edit, correcting alignment only.

Image 1: ORIGINAL LOCKED BACK TEMPLATE, 1024x1024. This is the sole target, with the exact required camera, mannequin, pose, blue color, body scale and background.
Image 2: APPROVED HELMET DESIGN seen from the BACK. Use its gray/gold helmet only. Its blue body is slightly shifted and MUST NOT be copied.

Add the helmet from image 2 to the head of image 1. Leave absolutely everything below y=343 and everything outside the helmet untouched from IMAGE 1. DO NOT redraw or reinterpret the blue mannequin. DO NOT shift, resize, relight, lengthen or widen any part of its body. Keep image 1's original gray background. Output ONE BACK image of exactly 1024 by 1024 pixels.

The original target's head crown is y=103, chin/back-head lower edge y=337, shoulders y=345, hands extend to x=151 and x=872 around y=532, feet end at y=921. These coordinates must stay fixed. The dome sits immediately over the original blue head with small clearance; gray/gold rear helmet extends from around y=98 to y=327, with symmetrical side guards reaching chin height y=336. Leave the original blue neck visible underneath. Cover the entire BACK of the blue skull with the continuous metal dome. This is a rear view, so no face or face opening. No floating or deeply embedded armor.

Keep helmet design exactly as shown in image 2: plain rounded neutral dark steel-gray shell, one broad muted antique-gold vertical center band across crown and down the back, broad gold lower edge, plain symmetric side guards. NO BLUE in helmet material. Clean smooth stylized surfaces, no grain, rivets, engraving, black outlines or hard specular highlights. Match original mold's soft lighting. No other armor, clothing, hair, weapons, shadows on the ground or text. Do not change the body to fit the helmet: fit only the helmet to the original, unchanged head. Preserve the original mold's entire non-helmet area.
